To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of PrRP in the brain was very limited to the dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus and the nucleus of the NTS, and that there was no change in the PrRP mRNA positive cell number in the NTS between different groups.
PrRP mRNA is localized in very restricted regions of the rat brain, and that the number of cells containing PrRP mRNA in NTS was not altered in pregnant rats.
the distribution of PrRP in the brain is restricted to the dorsomedial nucleus of the hypothalamus (DMH) and the nucleus of the tractus solitarious (NTS) of the medulla.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution and regulation of PrRP mRNA expression in the rat brain.
the distribution of PrRP in the rat brain and its possible physiological functions.
the distribution of PrRP in the rat brain and the relationship between the distribution and plasma prolactin concentration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PrRP neurons are located in the ventral part (ventrolateral nucleus) of the caudomedial hypothalamus and the caudal NTS.
PrRP mRNA is expressed in the NTS and the dorsomedial nucleus of the hypothalamus.
PrRP is expressed in the NTS, which may have an important role in the control of prolactin release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PrRP is a novel hypothalamic peptide, and that it is a candidate for a novel hypothalmo-pituitary prolactin releasing factor.
PrRP may be involved in the regulation of prolactin secretion and/or feeding behavior.
the hypothalamic PrRP mRNA is involved in the control of prolactin release and the PrRP mRNA in caudal NTS is involved in the regulation of the cardiovascular system.
